title: The General's Assessment
dialogue: General Brenner arrives without an aide. No briefing papers. He said he would give a soldier's view. He meant it.
monologue: No aide. No papers. That is either respect for my request or a test to see if I can hold a conversation without documents in front of me.

narrative.text: Honest picture. Northern border is adequately staffed but the equipment is aging — we are running on a five-year deferred maintenance cycle. The eastern garrison at Sevagrad is understaffed by about twelve percent. The officer corps is loyal to the Republic but there is a generational tension — younger officers came up under Halvek and were taught certain habits. Some of those habits are not compatible with civilian oversight.
What I need from you is clarity on the defense budget trajectory and a clear statement that civilian oversight means what it says. The men need to know which direction to face.

brenner_assessment.monologue: He said 'certain habits not compatible with civilian oversight' and left it there. That is a general telling a Chancellor that some of her officers are a problem without naming them. He is giving me information and asking me what I will do with it.

choices.text: "Civilian oversight means what it says, General. I expect the officer corps to understand that clearly."
"Which officers? I want names, General. If there is a loyalty problem in the corps I need to know specifically where it is."
